transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I came in because I’ve been doing things lately that don’t really make sense, and it’s starting to affect work and school. Like, at work I’m supposed to be dealing with receipts and numbers, normal stuff, but I’ll catch myself lining receipts across the floor instead of just sorting them. Not on a desk or in a folder—across the floor, like they have to go in a certain way, even though I can’t really explain why.

And sometimes with the calculator, I’ll tap it in sets of nine before I use it. It feels like I’m wasting time, but I keep doing it. I know that probably sounds strange. There was also this thing by the copier where I was just standing there with my hands held up, not really doing anything, until someone asked if I was okay. That was embarrassing, honestly.

So I guess I’m here because people are noticing, and I’m noticing too, and I don’t really know why I’m acting like that.
When you feel the need to line up the receipts or tap the calculator, does it happen because a distressing thought or fear is pushing you to do it?

I don’t think it’s exactly like a fear, no. It’s not like I’m thinking, “If I don’t tap the calculator nine times, something terrible will happen.” It’s more like… I just start doing it, and it feels like it has to be done in that moment, even though I can’t explain why.

Like with the receipts, I’m supposed to be sorting them for work, but then I’ll have them lined up across the floor, and part of me knows that’s not the normal way to do it. It’s not efficient, it doesn’t really help anything, and if someone walked in, which they have, it looks weird. But in the moment I’m just kind of caught up in arranging them.

Same with the calculator tapping. I’ll tap it in sets of nine before I use it, and it’s not because there’s some clear thought behind it. It’s just this thing I do, and then I realize I’ve wasted time. And the copier thing was even stranger because I was just standing there with my hands held up, not really doing anything, until someone asked if I was okay. So… no, I wouldn’t say there’s a specific distressing thought pushing it. It’s more that the behavior happens and only afterward I’m like, “Why did I do that?”
Have you been hearing voices that other people can’t hear?

Yeah… sometimes. I wasn’t sure if I should say that because it sounds bad when I say it out loud, but yes, there have been times where I hear a voice and I can’t find where it’s coming from.

It’s usually when I’m alone, like sitting at my desk, or sometimes when I’m walking home from class. It sounds like a man’s voice, and it’s clear enough that I’ll actually look around to see if someone said something to me. It’ll say things like, “check line seven,” or “you missed the sign.” Not like a vague thought in my head exactly—more like I heard it, like someone nearby said it.

And then I’ll stop and look around, because at first I think maybe a person behind me said something, or someone in another room, but there won’t be anyone there. That’s the part that makes me feel really uncomfortable, because I know if I tell people that, they’ll think I’m just making it up or being weird. But it has happened more than once.
Did these kinds of behaviors start in childhood?

I don’t really know. I mean, I don’t remember doing things exactly like this when I was a kid, not the receipt thing or tapping a calculator like that. I guess I had little habits like any kid, but nothing that people pointed out as strange, at least not that I can clearly remember.

It’s hard because when you ask “childhood,” I’m not sure what would count. Like, I don’t want to say no too confidently if maybe there were small things I just didn’t notice back then. But from what I remember, this kind of thing—where I get caught doing something odd and then realize other people are seeing it—that feels more recent to me. I don’t have a clear memory of it starting when I was young.
Do you currently have any beliefs that other people say aren’t true, but that you’re convinced are true?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I know how it sounds, and part of why I don’t usually say it is because when I try to explain it, people act like I’m just reading into things too much. But at work, with the invoices and account numbers and due dates, sometimes I get really convinced they’re not just normal entries.

Like, I’ll see a total on an invoice, or a due date, or the way an account number repeats, and it feels like it’s pointing at me somehow. Not just “oh, that’s a coincidence,” but like there’s a message in it, like it’s testing whether I’m noticing the pattern or whether I understand what I’m supposed to understand. And I’ll sit there looking at it way longer than I should, because it feels important, like if I miss it then that says something about me.

My supervisor has shown me before that the entries are normal, like they come from regular billing or whatever, and I can follow what he’s saying in the moment. I can see the spreadsheet and the source documents and all that. But even after that, I still have this feeling that the numbers are tracking me, or that someone is using them to see if I’m catching on. I know that sounds strange. I’m not saying everyone agrees with me. They don’t. But when it’s happening, it feels very hard to just dismiss it as nothing.
Have you found yourself feeling emotionally flat, like your face and voice show much less feeling than they used to?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t always notice it in the moment, but I’ve had people ask me if I’m bored or mad when I’m really not. Like my face just doesn’t do much, I guess, and my voice comes out kind of plain even if I’m trying to respond normally.

It’s not that I don’t care about people. I do. I’ll see texts from friends and I’ll think, “I should answer that,” but then I just let it sit there for hours, sometimes longer, and it feels like too much to make myself sound interested. After class, if people are going to hang out, I usually skip it now, even if part of me knows I probably would’ve liked it before.

And when friends talk about things I used to really get into, like music shows or art projects, I kind of just sit there. I can understand that it’s something I used to be excited about, but I don’t feel my face reacting much, and I don’t have much to say. It feels flat. Not like I hate it, just like the reaction doesn’t come up the way it used to.
Have you had other times when your body seemed stuck or held in an odd position and you couldn’t easily move out of it?

Yeah… sort of. I don’t know if I’d describe it exactly like I was “frozen,” because I wasn’t totally paralyzed or anything, but there have been times where I kind of get stuck in a position and don’t really move until someone snaps me out of it.

Like at work, I’ve stood by the copier with my hands held up—kind of awkwardly, like I was about to do something but then just stayed that way. I don’t even have a good reason for why. It’s not like I was stretching or pretending to hold something. I’d just be standing there, hands up, and then someone would ask, “Are you okay?” and only then I’d realize how weird it probably looked and put them down.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because it’s one thing if I’m doing something that has a purpose, but these moments don’t really make sense. Same with other stuff, like lining receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator in sets of nine. I know that’s not exactly my body being stuck, but it’s that same feeling of getting caught in something and not easily shifting out of it until someone interrupts me.
